chapters.loss: The loss: how surprised it was

description:
I trained a tiny AI from scratch on one graphics card. Three minutes ago it couldn't spell. Every chorus ends on what it really wrote after "ROMEO:", sung word for word: gibberish at step 100, half words at step 500, words at step 5,000.

How it learns: guess the next letter, see how wrong it was (that's the loss), nudge every weight a little, and do it again. 16,384 guesses a step, 5,000 steps, 81,920,000 guesses, 3.3 minutes on an RTX 3090.

The part I didn't plan: past step 2,000 it started learning the lines by heart. Its loss on the plays it practised kept falling, to 0.61. On a play it never read, the loss bottomed out at 1.47 and rose to 1.70.

{chapters}

The run: a 10,745,088-weight character-level GPT (6 layers, 6 heads, 384 wide, after nanoGPT's shakespeare_char recipe), trained from scratch on tiny Shakespeare (1,115,394 characters: 90% to practise on, 10% held back). Every number and every line of its writing on screen comes from that run.

ML, slowly: machine learning one idea at a time. #1 Downhill, #2 Tokens, #3 Meaning Is a Direction, #4 Who's It?, #5 this one. Next: Next Token, a big model writing, one token at a time.

Made with AI: the song is generated (ACE-Step 1.5), the visuals are rendered from code, the model and its numbers are real.

#MachineLearning #AI #LLM
